title: Best Throw Blankets 2026: Bedsure vs Barefoot Dreams
description: Five throw blankets compared on softness vs warmth, material (fleece, wool, knit), washability, and price — from the budget Bedsure fleece to the luxury Barefoot Dreams CozyChic.
lede: A throw blanket is an impulse-grade purchase that quietly becomes the most-used textile in your home — the one you reach for every evening on the sofa. The trade-off nobody spells out is softness versus warmth versus easy care: the plushest aren't always the warmest, and the warmest aren't always machine-washable.

sections.heading: Top pick: Bedsure Fleece Throw
paragraphs: The Bedsure Fleece Throw is the best throw blanket for most people because it nails the everyday essentials — genuinely soft, warm enough, completely machine-washable, and inexpensive enough to own several — without any fuss. It's a flannel/microfiber fleece that's plush and cosy against the skin, lightweight yet warm for sofa lounging and naps, and it comes in a huge range of colours and sizes so you can match any room. Crucially, it's fully machine washable and dryer-friendly, which matters enormously for the textile that catches snacks, pet hair, and spills nightly.

Its appeal is the combination of comfort, practicality, and price: it does exactly what a throw blanket needs to do — be soft, warm, and easy to clean — at a price low enough that you can have one on every sofa and not worry about the kids or the dog using it. Bedsure has become one of the best-selling throw brands precisely because these fleece throws deliver everyday cosiness and washability without costing much, and they hold up well to repeated washing.

The honest caveats: as a synthetic microfiber fleece it's not a luxury material or a heirloom piece, it's not as breathable as natural fibres (it can feel warm in summer), and it can attract some static and pet hair. But for the best balance of softness, warmth, easy washing, colour choice, and unbeatable value for an everyday sofa throw, the Bedsure is the default — the one to buy when you just want a great, practical, cosy blanket.

sections.heading: Most luxurious and the heritage wool pick: Barefoot Dreams CozyChic and Pendleton Wool
paragraphs: The Barefoot Dreams CozyChic is the luxury pick for unmatched plush softness — it's the blanket people describe as cloud-like and become obsessed with. Made from an ultra-soft proprietary synthetic microfiber knit, it's extraordinarily soft and plush against the skin, lightweight, and drapes beautifully, with a refined, slightly elevated look that suits being left out as a decorative throw. It's a cult favourite (and frequent luxury gift) precisely because the softness is genuinely a step above ordinary fleece. It's machine washable with care. The trade-offs are a steep price (several times a Bedsure), that the plush knit can shed or pill somewhat and needs gentle washing to preserve the texture, and that it prioritises softness over maximum warmth. But for the most luxurious, indulgent softness and a giftable premium throw, it's the standout.

The Pendleton Wool Throw is the heritage pick for genuine warmth, durability, and timeless style. Made from wool (often with iconic Pendleton patterns drawn from its century-plus weaving heritage), it's substantially warmer than synthetic fleece — wool is a superb natural insulator that stays warm even when damp and is naturally temperature-regulating and odour-resistant — and it's durable enough to last for decades and become a family heirloom. The distinctive Pendleton patterns make it a decorative statement as much as a functional blanket. It's the pick for someone who wants real, lasting warmth, natural fibres, and heritage style, and who'll invest in a blanket for life. The trade-offs are the premium price, that wool requires careful washing (often dry-clean or gentle hand-wash, not tumble-dry) and can feel less plush-soft than fleece against bare skin (and scratchy for the wool-sensitive). But for warmth, durability, and timeless character, it's unmatched.

Choose between them by what you value. The Barefoot Dreams wins on sheer plush softness and luxury indulgence. The Pendleton wins on real warmth, natural-fibre durability, and heritage style. The Barefoot Dreams is the cloud-soft splurge; the Pendleton the warm, lasting investment piece.

sections.heading: The value flannel and the trendy chunky knit: Utopia and Chunky Knit
paragraphs: The Utopia Flannel Throw is the rock-bottom value pick — a simple, soft flannel fleece throw at an even lower price than the Bedsure, for someone who wants cosy, washable warmth at the absolute minimum cost. It does the fundamental job: soft against the skin, warm enough for the sofa, fully machine washable, and available in basic colours and sizes. The material and longevity won't match nicer throws and it's plain rather than decorative, but for a cheap, practical, washable throw — for a kid's room, a spare blanket, a dorm, or just having extras around — it's the standout budget choice, often sold in multipacks. It's the no-frills 'just need a soft blanket' option.

The chunky knit throw is the trendy decorative pick for someone who wants their blanket to be a statement piece as much as a functional one. Chunky knit throws — thick, oversized hand-knit-look blankets, often in chenille or merino-blend yarn — have become hugely popular as styling pieces draped over a sofa or bed, adding cosy texture and a designer, Pinterest-worthy look to a room. They're warm and pleasantly weighty, and the chunky texture is visually striking. The trade-offs: they shed and can snag or stretch over time, many require careful hand-washing or spot-cleaning (the loose chunky weave doesn't always survive machine washing well), and they prioritise looks and texture over the easy practicality of a fleece. But for adding cosy, on-trend decorative texture to a room, the chunky knit is the stylish standout.

Choose by purpose. The Utopia wins as the cheapest practical, washable everyday throw. The chunky knit wins as a decorative, on-trend styling and texture piece. The Utopia is the budget workhorse; the chunky knit the Instagram-ready accent.

sections.heading: How to choose: material, softness vs warmth, washability, and size
paragraphs: Choose the material for the balance of softness, warmth, and care you want, because it drives everything. Synthetic fleece/microfiber (Bedsure, Barefoot Dreams, Utopia) is soft, cosy, affordable, and easy to machine-wash, but less breathable and not as warm as wool — ideal for everyday plush comfort and practicality. Wool (Pendleton) is the warmest, most durable, naturally temperature-regulating and odour-resistant, and lasts for decades, but costs more, needs careful washing, and can feel less plush or even scratchy. Knit/chenille (chunky knit) offers cosy texture and decorative style but sheds, snags, and often needs hand-washing. Decide whether you prioritise easy everyday comfort (fleece), maximum lasting warmth (wool), or decorative texture (knit).

Weigh softness against warmth, because they're not the same thing. The plushest, softest blankets (Barefoot Dreams, fleece) feel wonderful against the skin but are lightweight and prioritise cosy softness over heat; the warmest blankets (wool) insulate powerfully but may feel less cloud-soft. If your goal is sofa-lounging comfort and softness in a heated home, a plush fleece is ideal; if your goal is genuine warmth in a cold room or for someone who's always cold, wool's insulation wins even if it's less plush. A weighted blanket is a different category (for calming pressure rather than a casual throw). Match the softness-versus-warmth balance to whether you want indulgent comfort or real heat.

Prioritise washability and match the size to its use. Washability matters enormously for the textile that catches food, drinks, and pet hair nightly: fully machine-washable, dryer-friendly throws (the fleece options) are the easy, practical choice, while wool and chunky knits often need gentle hand-washing, dry-cleaning, or careful spot-cleaning that's less convenient for an everyday-use blanket — so if it'll see heavy daily use with kids and pets, prioritise machine-washability. On size, a standard throw (around 50x60 inches) suits one person on a sofa; larger sizes cover two people or drape a bed; pick the size for how you'll use it. Buy the material that fits your softness/warmth/care priorities, in a machine-washable form if it'll be used hard, and the right size for one person or shared use.

faqs.q: What's the difference between fleece, wool, and knit throw blankets?
faqs.a: They're different materials with distinct trade-offs in softness, warmth, and care. Synthetic fleece/microfiber (like the Bedsure, Barefoot Dreams, and Utopia) is soft, plush, cosy against the skin, lightweight, affordable, and fully machine-washable and dryer-friendly — the most practical everyday choice — but it's less breathable than natural fibres and not as warm as wool. Wool (like the Pendleton) is the warmest option and a superb natural insulator that stays warm even when damp, regulates temperature, resists odour, and lasts for decades, but it costs more, usually needs careful washing (often hand-wash or dry-clean rather than tumble-dry), and can feel less plush or even slightly scratchy against bare skin. Knit/chenille (chunky knit throws) offers cosy texture and a decorative, on-trend look and is pleasantly warm and weighty, but it sheds, can snag or stretch, and often needs gentle hand-washing rather than machine washing. In short: choose fleece for soft, easy, affordable everyday comfort; wool for maximum lasting warmth and durability; and knit for decorative texture and style. Many homes own a practical fleece throw for daily use and a nicer wool or knit piece for warmth or looks.

faqs.q: Are luxury throws like Barefoot Dreams worth the price?
faqs.a: It depends on how much you value softness and whether it's a gift or self-indulgence. Luxury throws like the Barefoot Dreams CozyChic genuinely are softer than ordinary fleece — the proprietary plush microfiber knit has a cloud-like, indulgent feel that people who own one consistently rave about, and it has a more refined, elevated look that suits being left out as a decorative piece. That softness is real and noticeable, which is why it's a hugely popular luxury gift. However, it costs several times as much as an excellent everyday fleece like the Bedsure, which is itself genuinely soft and warm and fully washable — so you're paying a large premium specifically for that extra step up in plushness and the brand cachet, not for better warmth (it's not warmer) or better practicality (the budget fleece is easier to wash). It can also shed or pill somewhat and needs gentler washing. So a luxury throw is worth it if you deeply value the ultimate in softness, want a premium gift, or like having an elevated decorative throw; but if you mainly want a soft, warm, practical, washable blanket for everyday use, an affordable fleece delivers the large majority of the comfort for a fraction of the price.

faqs.q: Can I machine wash a throw blanket?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on the material, and this is worth checking before you buy if easy care matters to you. Synthetic fleece and microfiber throws (like the Bedsure and Utopia) are fully machine washable and dryer-friendly — you can wash them frequently on a normal cycle, which makes them ideal for the everyday-use blanket that constantly catches food, drinks, and pet hair. Plush microfiber-knit luxury throws (like the Barefoot Dreams) are usually machine washable but need gentler care — cold water, gentle cycle, low or air dry, and no fabric softener — to preserve their plush texture and prevent excess shedding. Wool throws (like the Pendleton) generally should not be machine washed and tumble-dried, as wool can shrink, felt, and lose its shape — they typically require hand-washing in cool water or dry-cleaning, which is less convenient for daily use. Chunky knit throws often need hand-washing or careful spot-cleaning too, since the loose weave can stretch and snag in a machine. So if you want a throw you can toss in the wash without thinking — for a home with kids and pets especially — choose a machine-washable fleece; if you choose wool or knit for their warmth or looks, accept that they need more careful, less frequent cleaning.
